text:
incident-bot: Pager: sudden increase in GPU OOMs on decode/streaming fleet (svc-decode-us-east). Error signature: CUDA out-of-memory during decode loop. Started ~2026-03-15T12:03:20Z. Current symptom: ~3-4% request drops, several node restarts, tail latency spikes. Paging primary oncall @ryan and secondary @sara.
ryan: I’m oncall, jumping in. pulling recent crashlogs now. any customer hits identified yet?
cs-rep: received two SEV reports from customers: intermittent truncated streaming responses and reconnects. one customer reports partial responses when long `max_tokens` used.
sara: quick read: decode pods show repeated `CUDA error: out of memory` during streaming generation when sequences > 1024. KV cache growth + unbounded client max_tokens appears correlated.
mike: logs show this on node host gpu-047 and gpu-048, container restart loop observed. kernel logs show GPU memory fragmentation warnings. snippet: ```
E decode_worker.cpp:421 - CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 1.2GB for attention_kv
E runtime.cpp:77 - allocate_kv_cache failed, aborting stream
```
oncall-bot: Running the standard OOM playbook: 1) cap incoming max_tokens at proxy, 2) enable fallback model variant (quantized) for streaming, 3) drain affected nodes, 4) open customer update.
ryan: applying immediate mitigation: pushing a temporary proxy rule to clamp `max_tokens` to 512 for streaming route `svc-decode-stream-v2`. will roll back per incident postmortem. command: ```bash
# api call to routing control
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/routing/limits -d '{"route":"svc-decode-stream-v2","max_tokens":512}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```
sara: good. also enabling automatic fallback to `rdl-small-quant` for any request that hits memory pressure. edit in console under model routing -> add fallback list.
mike: starting a graceful drain of gpu-047, gpu-048: cordon + evict decode pods. doing one node at a time to avoid capacity cliff. ```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-047 && kubectl drain gpu-047 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
katie: customer-success: I posted a short note to the two affected customers, telling them we’re throttling large token requests temporarily and working on fix. asking for any logs they can share. :thumbsup:
ryan: I’m also flipping on the per-request KV cache eviction heuristic in runtime to limit per-session KV to 6k tokens (soft limit). quick patch rolled to 5% of decode fleet to test. snippet of config: ```json
{"kv_cache": {"session_token_soft_limit": 6000, "eviction_policy": "lru"}}
```
mike: after drain, node gpu-047 memory stabilized, no further OOMs in last 3 min. gpu-048 still having intermittent failures, evicting now.
sara: noticed some clients sending `max_tokens: 10000` via streaming handshake; proxy clamp should drop those but need telemetry to block abusive clients. added a rate limiter rule to upstream for requests with `max_tokens>2000`.
oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-2167770000-stream-decode. Recommend follow-up actions: permanent limit policy, improved KV cache heuristics, add test for long streaming sequences.
ryan: root-cause hypothesis: misconfigured client defaults + missing per-route token caps allowed runaway generation that exhausts GPU memory via KV cache growth. secondary: fragmentation + long-running sessions prevented allocator from reusing memory efficiently.
katie: CS will coordinate follow-up with customers; we told them we expect resolution within 2 hours and will send an ETA update in 30m.
mike: post-mitigation metrics: request drops back to ~0.2%, tail latency improving. collecting per-pod GPU memory utilization for the last 2 hours and will attach to pager ticket.
ryan: blocking TODOs before declaring incident mitigated: 1) complete drain of remaining bad nodes, 2) confirm fallback flow succeeded for streaming traffic, 3) push a short-term config enforce to clamp `max_tokens` at edge for all streaming routes, 4) create follow-up issue for runtime-level KV cache compaction.
sara: putting together a small patch for allocator to prefer reusing freed GPU buffers earlier — will ship to canary 10% and monitor.
cs-rep: customers acknowledged the update and requested a short write-up once we have root cause.
ryan: handing off to @sara for next shift ops at 12:55Z — I've documented actions in the incident ticket and left the console in throttled state. tagging @katie for the customer update. oncall status: resolved for now but in watch for 45m. :white_check_mark:
